Distinct nearby waters and river context distinguish them. The complete ring overlays show extensive shoreline generalization, filled islands and omitted thin arms; detailed whole-lake coverage is not established.

observations.own_observations: Map page 6 directly labels Clearwater Lake over its rounded main basin and northern bays, with Cormorant Lake only partly visible to the northeast. Page 9 repeats the Clearwater Lake label in a land-use map. Both support Clearwater correspondence while showing detail lost in the generalized ring. The park maps were not geometrically registered for this review.

complete_feature_observations.independent_observation: The direct blue Kississing Lake label identifies the water with a broad island-studded central basin, northwestern lobe, elongated northeastern arm and two narrow southern lobes. The complete selected ring follows this arrangement. Islands are filled and detailed narrow arms and peninsula margins are generalized. Kisseynew Lake is separately labelled south beyond the ring; Kississing River is river context, not an alternative lake identity. No differently named lake is implicated by the selected generalized footprint on this inspected map. Exact river/lake transition and detailed named extent remain unverified.

The complete ring surrounds the rounded main Clearwater Lake basin with a projecting northern arm and indented eastern shore, west of the road/rail corridor and south/southwest of Cormorant. The geological original directly labels the basin, and park map pages 6 and 9 confirm the same water and detailed bays/islands. The long straight generalized northern edge omits fine bays and islands, the southwestern and southern margin omits small shoreline extensions, and the southeast projection is simplified. Root and Reader lakes lie separately west/southwest. Cormorant is a distinct lake northeast, and named internal bays are not additional whole-lake names.

The complete ring follows the broad east-west northern main Cormorant basin, an eastern hook separated by a peninsula, and the wider south-central lobe. Cormorant Lake is directly labelled on the original. Long thin northern/northwestern extensions and intricate shore margins extend beyond the selected ring; islands are filled and the northeast/eastern shore is substantially smoothed. Clearwater Lake lies separately southwest, Mawdesley Lake south/southeast, and North Moose Lake farther east outside the selected ring. The park map supplies only the Cormorant-Clearwater adjoining context and not the entire Cormorant extent.
